clue.text: I'm surprised Kay's on fiddle

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another follows it here as an added piece

parts.note: a coo is an exclamation of surprise, as in 'Coo, look at that!'
Kay is the spoken name of the letter K

explanation.surface: Someone startled to learn that Kay is playing the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is a British exclamation of mild surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books is to fiddle them, falsifying accounts dishonestly.

clue.text: Corporation has pan for meat dish

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, also called a pot belly
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly, to roast it

explanation.surface: A large company has a cooking pan to make a meal of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is a big belly; 'pan' looks like cookware but is a verb, to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of beef braised slowly in a covered pot is a classic meat dish.

clue.text: Wife abroad? Cheat endlessly!

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word for a cheat drops off

parts.note: a cheat or impostor is a fraud

explanation.surface: An exclamation accusing a spouse overseas of infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: German for a wife or married woman, so a wife in a foreign country, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fancy up-ending Fido off Lake Bloomer

indicators.note: turning on end in a down clue, so the word for a fancy is read bottom to top

parts.note: a fancy or passing craze is a fad

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A dog named Fido is fancifully tipped off the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-ending' turns FAD into DAF; 'off' rearranges FIDO plus L into FODIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is anything that blooms, a flower, and the spring daffodil is one example.

clue.text: Complaint: medical department running smoothly!

parts.note: a complaint is an illness, such as influenza
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient's grumble that a hospital ward is working without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' means an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or motion that flows easily and smoothly without stumbling is said to be fluent.

clue.text: Carriage ring replaced by one division in France

indicators.note: says one letter is swapped out and another letter stands in its place

parts.note: carriage in the sense of bearing or posture is deportment
a ring is round, like the letter O
A means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A railway carriage has one ring swapped out somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a train, but means posture.
explanation.definitionFit: France is divided administratively into numbered regions each called a département.

clue.text: Celebrated striker very important to nameless left-wing MP once

parts.note: big can mean important, as in 'a big decision'

indicators.note: N is short for name, so one N is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Tony Benn was a famous left-wing Labour MP

explanation.surface: A star footballer is linked to a long-dead socialist politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football; it is the Westminster clock, which strikes the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bell in the clock tower at Westminster, famous for striking the hours, is a celebrated striker.

clue.text: Say "heartlessly merry" describes a foolish-looking person's face?

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word for merry is removed

parts.note: gay in its older sense means merry or cheerful

explanation.surface: A comment that a joyless reveller has a foolish face.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone made to look foolish is said to have egg on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Having egg on your face means looking foolish, so such a face could jokingly be described as covered in egg.

clue.text: Ring determined to acquire repute

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
dour can mean stern and obstinately determined

explanation.surface: A gang set on gaining a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: To be in good or bad odour with someone is to have that reputation with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour in the sense of standing or reputation, as in the idiom 'in bad odour'.

clue.text: Alien's leg fitted with 360° vision?

indicators.note: assembled and fitted together, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the word with its S kept as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A space creature's limb is equipped to see in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted' rearranges ALIENS and LEG; the possessive S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision through a full circle of 360 degrees would let a creature see everything around it.

clue.text: King, getting Queen fine dish, so avoided commotion

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the word just named is left out, removed from the dish

parts.note: a soufflé is a baked egg dish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch, served a fancy dish by his queen, steered clear of a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a British informal word for a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: One was set up for men in order to change baby without embarrassment, initially

definitions.text: One was set up for men

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the next piece
to change something is to alter it, so the letters are reordered
the first letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: Changing a baby without blushing is the task described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges BABY to ABBY; 'without' (outside) puts it round the E from 'embarrassment, initially'. 'change baby' looks like nappy duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery, a religious house founded for monks, that is for men.

clue.text: Front of car fitted with lights and immobilised

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lamped means supplied with lamps

explanation.surface: A car's bonnet given new headlights, and then wheel-clamped.
explanation.walkthrough: Clamping is the British practice of locking a wheel of an illegally parked car.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamped car has a wheel lock fitted and cannot be driven away, so it is immobilised.

clue.text: Having something up top makes one plump for the table

definitions.meaning: wearing a hat, read as two words
a castrated cockerel fattened for eating

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a castrated, fattened cockerel; and, split in two, wearing a cap.

clue.text: On with pet irritant: member of circus in much reduced circumstances

definitions.text: member of circus in much reduced circumstances

parts.note: an actor who is on is performing on stage
a flea irritates a pet dog or cat

explanation.surface: A ruined circus artist now working with a pet's itch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much reduced circumstances' looks like poverty but means tiny size: a flea circus.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flea circus the trained artistes are insects, so the members are drastically reduced in size.

clue.text: star@alien set back by infectious disease

indicators.note: set backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: the sun is a star
the @ symbol is read as at
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: An email address for an extraterrestrial is foiled by an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' reverses SUN AT ET, the clue's email address read out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a serious bacterial infection that enters through wounds.

clue.text: Sailors' purgative?

definitions.meaning: Epsom ... are taken as a laxative

explanation.definitionFit: The same word gives veteran seamen and a mineral laxative such as Epsom salts.

clue.text: Look round the stereotypically Yorkshire cell

indicators.note: placed around, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
in a stereotyped Yorkshire accent 'the' is clipped to t'

explanation.surface: Peering about a prison cell in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire dialect is caricatured as saying t' for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is old British criminal slang for a prison cell, and also for a safe.

clue.text: Lap part of a garment

definitions.meaning: one stage of a race or journey
one tube of a pair of trousers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a stage of a journey and also the part of trousers covering a limb.

clue.text: Legs said to crumple in controlled descent

indicators.note: to crumple is to collapse out of shape, so the letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A skier's legs reportedly gave way on the way down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: In mountaineering, a glissade is a controlled slide down a snow slope.

clue.text: Put out energy on cross to power overhead railway

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a cross is shaped like the letter X
P is the symbol for power
the El is the elevated railway in Chicago or New York

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiring an elevated train line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'El' is the American name for an elevated city railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to put them out, as from a school or club.

clue.text: Act like a younger Schwarzenegger with dancing shoe? Smooth!

parts.note: a pump is a light shoe worn for dancing
to iron is to smooth out creases

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder with dance shoes is called a smooth mover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' looks like an anagram indicator but is part of the shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting weights is called pumping iron, and young Arnold Schwarzenegger was a champion bodybuilder.

clue.text: Sun backing topless model deal? Rupert's in his element here!

indicators.note: moving backwards, so the shortened word is reversed
with its top, the first letter, taken off

parts.note: the newspaper's name taken as written
the Model T Ford gives the letter T
deal is pine or fir timber, that is wood

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper supporting a contract with a topless model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops S from SUN, leaving UN, which 'backing' turns to NU. The surface plays on Rupert Murdoch, owner of the Sun, and its topless models.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutwood is the village where the cartoon character Rupert Bear lives, so it is his home ground.

clue.text: Swinging yodeller — 24 31's was deficient, as 17 1 pointed out in the 18 6

definitions.text: Swinging yodeller — 24 31's was deficient, as 17 1 pointed out in the 18 6

parts.words: Swinging yodeller — 24 31's was deficient, as 17 1 pointed out in the 18 6
parts.note: a jungle hero swinging through trees, famous for his yell, and the comedy sketch in which a one-legged actor auditions for that role

explanation.surface: A comic recalls a famous sketch about an actor with a missing limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Peter Cook and Dudley Moore sketch, Moore plays a one-legged man auditioning for a two-legged jungle role; Cook says his right leg is deficient.
explanation.definitionFit: The jungle hero swings on vines and gives a yodelling cry, and the sketch has a one-legged actor going for the part.

clue.text: The old Queen's favourite borough

definitions.meaning: Robert, Earl of Leicester, favourite of Elizabeth I
a metropolitan borough in the West Midlands of England

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Elizabeth I's favourite courtier is also the name of a West Midlands town.

clue.text: Breathes, so constricting medium neck

parts.note: whatever breathes lives, that is, it is

indicators.note: squeezing around, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: thus means so, therefore
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A breathing patient whose medium-sized neck is being squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' looks anatomical but is a neck of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining two larger areas, a neck of land.

clue.text: Wives/partners collectively live away from part of Manhattan

indicators.note: taken away from, so the next letter is removed from that word

parts.note: Harlem is a neighbourhood in northern Manhattan
L marks the live wire in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Spouses living away from a New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives or concubines belonging to one man, taken collectively.

clue.text: Cooker part? Ring itinerant workman

parts.note: a hob is the top of a cooker with the burners
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cooker part is ringing a travelling workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as a cooker's gas ring, but it is O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American term for a migrant worker who travels looking for work.

clue.text: Lack of faith in how rapper Viking explorer might be heard to introduce himself?

indicators.text: might be heard to introduce himself
indicators.note: said aloud by way of introduction, so the answer matches the sound of his words

parts.note: a rapper's 'Dis be Leif', meaning 'this is Leif', with Leif Ericson the Norse explorer

explanation.surface: Imagining a Norse adventurer announcing himself in hip-hop slang.
explanation.walkthrough: Leif Ericson was a Viking said to have reached North America; 'dis be' is street speech for 'this is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief is a refusal or inability to believe, a lack of faith.

clue.text: Oscar's equivalent of a burglar tool (not jack)

indicators.note: without, so the letter for jack is removed

parts.note: a jemmy is a short crowbar used by burglars
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A thief's crowbar described without a jack, as if comparing awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' tempts as NATO alphabet O, but is the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television award, the small-screen counterpart of the film Oscar.

clue.text: See 14
Far from clever to put black pelt, perhaps, on old hat

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
to pelt is to rain hard; 'perhaps' marks it as one sense
something old hat is out of date, dead

explanation.surface: Putting an animal skin on an old hat would be stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' looks like fur but is the verb for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Braindead is an informal insult for someone extremely stupid, far from clever.

clue.text: Captain Bobby's last low note

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A football captain's final note is a deep one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Moore captained England to the 1966 World Cup; 'last' means his last name. 'low' is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The England captain Bobby's surname, his last name, completes his famous name.
